digest.component_or_area: error code classification and diagnostic mapping
propositions: The blanket LLMError → llm_unavailable classification fallthrough incorrectly labels non-availability failures (input rejection, budget exhaustion, context window exceeded, structured output errors) as provider outages, causing LLM/agent consumers to misdiagnose and act on wrong remediation paths.

The _structured_llm_failure function hardcodes error=llm_unavailable for every LLMError across four MCP gate tools instead of deriving the code from exception type via error_code_for, preventing per-subclass routing from applying uniformly.

The coverage.llm_unavailable boolean is set True for both genuine LLMUnavailableError outages and LLMInputRejectedError input rejections, overloading the signal name and misleading three readers (drift_floor.py, orchestrator.py, review_bot/adapter.py) about the actual failure mode.

The reconciled taxonomy (from landed epic dbca-97ac-ad96-4d6d) preserves workflow caller-input codes (not_found, invalid_input) and bare-base llm_unavailable, requiring that only the LLMRunnerError subtree be rerouted from llm_unavailable to the accurate-but-broad command_failed.

An exhaustive exception-to-code contract test encoding the reconciled taxonomy and a vocabulary-closure test asserting all emitted codes are registered would prevent future subclasses from silently inheriting the misleading llm_unavailable fallthrough.
